page: Microsoft Azure L80as_v5 is a storage-optimized virtual machine built on an AMD x86_64 processor architecture and managed via the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The instance is configured with 80 dedicated vCPUs and 640.0 GB of system memory, maintaining an 8.0 GB per-core ratio. The server does not bundle hardware GPU accelerators, directing its computational focus toward high-concurrency multi-threaded CPU tasks and memory-resident processing.

A central architectural element of the L80as_v5 is its direct-attached storage subsystem, which features 19,199 GB of local NVMe SSD space alongside support for Premium Storage. This design provides massive local storage capacity with minimal latency, eliminating network bandwidth constraints typical of remote block volumes. However, as local NVMe storage on cloud instances is ephemeral, architectures using this server must implement redundancy and persistent backup strategies to mitigate the risk of host-level data loss.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the instance provides high resource density by packing 80 dedicated compute cores, large memory, and expansive NVMe SSD capacity into a single operational unit. This configuration reduces the operational overhead and networking costs associated with managing multiple smaller cluster nodes. The hardware profile is optimized for storage-intensive enterprise workloads, including high-throughput transactional databases, distributed NoSQL engines, data warehousing, and big data analytics pipelines.
description: Microsoft Azure L80as_v5 is a storage-optimized virtual machine instance powered by an AMD x86_64 processor. Running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor, the server provides 80 dedicated vCPUs alongside 640.0 GB of memory, yielding an 8.0 GB per-core allocation. A defining architectural characteristic is its inclusion of 19,199 GB of integrated local NVMe SSD storage, paired with Premium Storage support to facilitate high-throughput, low-latency disk operations without relying exclusively on remote volumes. The instance does not feature dedicated GPU accelerators or complimentary public IPv4 addresses. By consolidating vast local disk capacity with substantial computational density and high memory reserves, the configuration avoids network storage bottlenecks for extreme disk I/O demands. Consequently, the L80as_v5 is engineered specifically for large transactional database management systems, distributed NoSQL databases, data warehousing platforms, and big data analytics pipelines requiring significant continuous throughput.
